ideas.title: The woodblock press
ideas.goal: The player carves their own stamp into a block of wood with a gouge, inks it, and presses it onto paper, a wall, a sail or a friend's back. The print is exactly what they carved, mirrored, and it stays. Fun: making a mark of your own, and the surprise of the mirror image when the paper comes off.
ideas.idea: A small press and a bench by the workshop. The block is a heightfield (512x512) that the gouge really cuts: each stroke removes material along its path, deeper where you press, and chips fly off. The roller lays ink only on the high parts, and the print transfers where block and surface touch under pressure, so a bump in the block or an uneven push gives a pale, broken print. Prints become decals that stay on whatever they were pressed on. Someone watching sees Lumi carve, the black ink roll on, and the paper peeled back slowly to show the picture.
ideas.form: Plugin (press, block, gouge, decals that are saved), with the carving and inking on Mantle kernels. Traced film: carve, ink, peel.

ideas.title: Smoke rings
ideas.goal: The player blows smoke rings across the island: aim them, make two rings leapfrog through each other, blow out a lantern from 10 m away, push a firefly off course, send a ring through a friend's open beak. Fun: a skill shot with a soft, slow projectile that you can watch the whole way.
ideas.idea: Real vortex-ring dynamics: each ring is a vortex filament (a loop of a few hundred points) moving by its own Biot-Savart induced velocity on the GPU, so rings travel, slow down, wobble, and a following ring shrinks, speeds up, slips through the one ahead and then swaps with it. They break up against trees and walls. The smoke is a real volume in the path tracer (a participating medium lit by the lanterns), and the ring's flow pushes light things: leaves, flames, fireflies.
ideas.form: Plugin (key R while jumped in), a vortex filament solver on Mantle, smoke as a Hikari medium. Traced night film: two rings leapfrog and blow out a lantern.

ideas.title: Leaf boats down the stream
ideas.goal: The player and the creatures drop leaf boats into the stream at the top of the hill and race them down to the sea. The flow decides who wins: eddies behind rocks trap boats, the fast water on the outside of a bend carries them past. Fun: choosing where to launch, poking your boat free with a stick, cheering.
ideas.idea: A real stream: shallow-water equations on a grid along the stream bed (GPU), fed by a spring, flowing around stones the player can move to change the current. Boats are floating bodies dragged by the local flow and pushed by the wind, and they bump each other. Someone watching sees bright leaves spinning in eddies and four creatures running along the bank.
ideas.form: A new stream in the terrain and a plugin (shallow-water solver on Mantle, boats, race and finish line). Traced film from the water's surface following one boat.

ideas.title: The potter's wheel and the kiln
ideas.goal: The player throws a pot on a spinning wheel by pressing with both hands, fires it in the kiln and uses it: a vase for flowers, a bowl for berries, a bell. Too thin a wall slumps on the wheel, or cracks in the fire. Fun: a craft you get better at, and every pot is your own.
ideas.idea: The clay is an axisymmetric profile of rings that keep their volume: pressing in moves clay up, pulling up thins the wall, and spinning too fast flings the rim out (centrifugal force against how stiff wet clay is). The kiln heats the pot over time; a wall with uneven thickness cracks where the thermal stress is highest. Glazes are real Hikari coated materials: glossy, crackled, translucent at the rim. Someone watching sees the clay rise between Lumi's wings and the kiln's orange glow.
ideas.form: Plugin (wheel, kiln, pots as real props with a mesh built from the profile), clay and heat on the GPU. Path traced still of the glazed pots on a shelf, film of a throw.

ideas.title: Thin ice
ideas.goal: On a frozen morning the player skates across the sea ice to a small islet with a gift, and the ice is thin in places. It creaks and whitens under you, cracks spread, and a crack you start is still there on the way back. Fun: risk, reading the ice, and the sound and look of a crack running away from your feet.
ideas.idea: The glass sea project's next step: the ice becomes a real plate (thickness varies, thinner where the current runs) that bends under the skater's weight. Where the stress passes a limit a crack runs along the stress field and branches. Skates have low friction along the blade and high across it, so turns carve. Cracks are real refractive cuts in the traced ice, with dark water under them.
ideas.form: Extending the glasssea plugin with a plate and fracture solver on Mantle. Traced morning film: crossing, a crack chasing the skater.

ideas.title: Hide and seek in the dark, by clapping
ideas.goal: At night the friends hide, and the player can only find them by clapping: the clap lights up the island the way the sound found it, and a friend behind a bush shows up as a gap and a warm echo. Each clap wakes the owl a little more. Fun: a hunt by sound, and deciding when to risk one more clap.
ideas.idea: The island echo project's next step and its goal: the live clap uses the full scene (trees, hedges, friends' bodies, not only the terrain) via Raycore on the GPU. Friends make soft sounds back, and the owl hears every clap through the owl ears code. Three rounds, with a time limit in owl wakefulness.
ideas.form: Mini game (plugin) joining nightclap and owlears. Traced night film of one round.

ideas.title: Sailing upwind
ideas.goal: The player sails a small boat around three buoys and has to learn to tack against the wind: trim the sail too tight and the boat heels and stalls, too loose and the sail flaps. Fun: the moment you understand how to go upwind, and racing the creatures' boat.
ideas.idea: The sail is real cloth (PrintSim sheet) in the island's wind field. Its lift and drag come from the actual angle between sail and wind, the keel resists sideways slip, and the hull heels, rolls and makes a wake in the water. Someone watching sees the sail fill with a snap after a tack.
ideas.form: Plugin (boat, sail, buoys, race), cloth on Mantle. Traced film from a low camera on the water.

ideas.title: Bees that tell each other where the flowers are
ideas.goal: The player plants flowers to steer a beehive: bees fly out, find the flowers, come home and dance to tell the others, and the swarm moves where the player planted. Honey fills the hive, and the player smokes the bees to calm them before taking it. Friends who poke the hive get chased. Fun: steering a living swarm without touching it.
ideas.idea: A foraging simulation: each bee has a crop of nectar, a memory of the best patch and an energy budget; returning bees do a waggle dance whose angle and length encode direction and distance, and the bees watching it fly that way. Flowers really refill over time. Hundreds of bees on the GPU, with the dance visible on the comb.
ideas.form: Plugin (hive, bees, honey, the smoker), a new hive asset. Traced close-up film of the dance on the comb and the swarm going out.

ideas.title: Lumi learns the unicycle
ideas.goal: The player rides a unicycle as Lumi: lean to go, pedal to catch the fall, wobble, fall over, try again, until they can ride the path round the island. Lumi gets better each time it rides (its balance improves from practice). Fun: a hard balance skill with funny falls, and seeing Lumi learn.
ideas.idea: A real inverted pendulum on a wheel: the wheel, the seat and Lumi's body are rigid bodies with joints (PrintSim), Lumi's wings and pedalling are motors driven by the player plus a controller that learns from each ride. Falls are physical: the unicycle runs off, Lumi tumbles and gets up.
ideas.form: Plugin and a new self-skill for Lumi, a generated unicycle asset. Traced film: wobbling, a fall, then a clean ride.

ideas.title: Soapbox carts down the hill
ideas.goal: The player and three creatures each build a cart from parts (planks, wheels, a sail, a box) and race down the island hill. Heavy carts are fast but crash on the bend, big wheels jump the roots. Fun: building, then the crash.
ideas.idea: Each cart is real rigid bodies and joints: wheels with friction on the terrain, axles that can break, and the creature riding as a body that falls off. The build changes mass, centre of mass and grip, so the build decides the race.
ideas.form: Mini game plugin with a parts bench, rigid bodies on Mantle. Traced race film.
